claim: Let \((X,\mathcal X,\mu,T_1,\ldots,T_\ell)\) be a measure-preserving system in which \(H=\langle T_1,\ldots,T_\ell\rangle\) is 2-step nilpotent and its commutator subgroup \([H,H]\) is finite. Assume every \(T_i\) is totally ergodic. For independent polynomials \(p_1,\ldots,p_\ell\in\mathbb Z[n]\) and bounded functions \(f_1,\ldots,f_\ell\), one has \[\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}T_i^{p_i(n)}f_i\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^{\ell}\int f_i\,d\mu\] in \(L^2(\mu)\). Thus the independent-polynomial joint-ergodicity conjecture of Koutsogiannis--Kuca--Sun holds for every 2-step nilpotent action whose commutator subgroup is finite.
integrity: The proof is an exact finite-index reduction using the exponent of the finite central commutator subgroup, followed by the published commuting independent-polynomial joint-ergodicity theorem. No numerical experiment or external certificate is used.
scientific_limitations: Infinite commutator subgroups, including genuinely Heisenberg-type actions, are not covered.
The statement proves the product-limit conclusion under total ergodicity, not the stronger non-totally-ergodic seminorm estimate.
A residual originality risk is that this finite-commutator reduction may have appeared implicitly as folklore about virtually abelian actions.
title: Finite commutators reduce independent nilpotent polynomial averages to the commuting case
